The dependency graph is an #include graph, not a call graph. graft callers --depth 2 was run against the modules under test and returned no indexed cross-file call edges for any symbol probed, so the finer relation was not available. The include graph over-states coupling where a header is included for a type, and misses dispatch through function pointers and macros. It is the conservative direction for ordering but it is not the same relation a call graph would give.

graft reported each probed symbol as defined twice, once in the .c and once in the .h, and drops cross-file callers of an ambiguous name rather than guessing. That is a second, independent reason the tool could not supply a call graph.
The 38 HL_* interface headers are counted from the halcogen_via_module_under_test field of the recorded run, which reflects the tree at the time of the run, not the current tree.
Fan-in and fan-out figures count distinct modules including a module, not call sites, and are not weighted by which header was included for which reason.

The order is a reverse topological order of an acyclic module graph. Cycles that exist at file level within a layer, the database with ftask and os with ftask header-sharing pairs, are handled by integrating the pair together, which is a judgement rather than a derivation.
No integration test specification exists, so no step here has an oracle. An order without oracles is a schedule.

defect_handling.evidence_of_real_defects_found: The recorded sweep did find real product defects, and they were classified rather than smoothed: 6 out-of-bounds array index, 4 macro arity, 2 implicit function declaration, 2 implicit int, 1 absolute-value truncation, 1 excess initialisers, 1 tautological guard, plus 8 undeclared identifier - 17 files failing to build on a product defect, plus 8 undeclared-identifier failures the classifier treats as a separate class. REATTRIBUTION.md in the run directory is the re-attribution of the build failures, and TASK1-CLASSIFICATION.md records a specific product defect found by an experiment that was then reverted. A dead-write product defect was removed in commit 176fe234. These are real findings from real runs, which is why the severity model above has evidence behind it rather than being invented.
defect_handling.regression_trigger: Any change to a module with fan-in above 10 triggers its full inbound regression set. That threshold comes from the measured fan-in ranking: foxmath at 43, os at 40, database at 39, can_helper at 38, diag at 32, ftask at 22, bms at 17.
defect_handling.retention: Every integration defect keeps the before and after pair of recorded runs, the exact level and step, and the modules joined. The run directory's pattern of a baseline result file, an after result file and a classifier output is the model.
defect_handling.retest_rule: Re-run the failing boundary first, then the regression set for the level, then every test that includes a module on the changed path. A defect is not closed on a single re-run; it is closed when the level's full regression set is green twice, because the recorded run demonstrates that classifier output is stable but says nothing about test stability under repetition.
routes: Interface disagreements route to the layer with the higher fan-in, because it is the one whose change costs more.
Defects in a shared AFE layer route to the shared layer, never to each vendor variant.
Defects found by the real-defect build-failure classes route to the existing finding records, not to a new integration defect, because they are already classified.
severity_model: S1 interface defect: two modules disagree about a data-block layout, a signature or a diagnostic id. Action: stop the level, route to the interface owner, and treat as a configuration-management event if a layout changed, because app/config reaches 29 layers.
S2 propagation defect: a value is produced correctly and lost or corrupted between two layers. Action: fix at the boundary, re-run the producing module's regression before the consuming one.

S3 substitution artefact: a defect that exists only because the host substitutes for hardware. Action: record it as a substitution artefact and do not fix it in the product. This class exists because 22 build failures are clang-only diagnostics and 1 is a macOS object-format limitation, and fixing those in the product would be wrong.
S4 uncovered integration: two modules have no test that exercises them together. Action: this is a gap, not a defect, and it routes to FB2-MAN-VDR-000001.

dependency_basis.derivation: #include graph over src/. 263 translation units scanned (src/app/**/*.c plus src/bootloader/**/*.c at tree commit ebd6d5a6); 209 have at least one intra-source include edge. Edge rule, stated so a reader can re-run it and get the same numbers: take each .c's own quoted #include directives, resolve each named header to a sibling .c owning that header stem, and drop the edge when the target is the including file itself. Two conventions follow from that rule and account for the ranking below. First, where a stem exists in both trees - foxmath and can_helper do - the src/app copy owns the stem, so a src/bootloader copy's own #include of its own header resolves to the src/app copy and registers as a real inbound edge; this is why foxmath reads 43 rather than 42 and can_helper 38 rather than 37. Second, a stem's count is reported on every path that carries that stem, which is why the two foxmath paths and the two can_helper paths each show the same number. Fan-in is the count of distinct modules including a module; fan-out is the count of distinct modules it includes. The integration order is the reverse topological order of this graph, which is well defined because the graph is acyclic at module granularity - the only cycles present are file-level and are the database/ftask and os/ftask pairs that share a header, not a compile-time loop. Revision 1 published 191 translation units with an edge; that figure is reproduced by neither this rule nor a transitive-header variant, which yields 240, so 209 is published here as the value the stated rule produces. The ten fan-in entries were re-derived under this rule and all ten match. verify_swe5_swe6.py in the run evidence directory re-derives the whole graph, checks all ten entries and re-checks the 209; it does not import corpus.py.

fan_in_ranking.role_in_order: Step 1. Highest fan-in in the application tree and a leaf in practice: 43 modules include it and nothing in the graph obliges it to be integrated after anything. Integrating it first means 43 later steps have one fewer unknown.
Step 1, alongside the application copy. The two are separate translation units with the same fan-in.

Step 2. The OS abstraction. It is the module the whole task model hangs off, and it is the one place a host build most obviously diverges from the product, because the host substitutes a POSIX implementation for the FreeRTOS one.
Step 2. The data-block store. Almost every layer talks to it, so its read, write and notify semantics must be settled before any producer or consumer is integrated against it.
Step 3. CAN pack and unpack helper shared by every CAN callback, RX and TX.
Step 3. The diagnostic engine. 32 modules raise events through it, so its event routing and debounce contract has to be fixed before any producer is judged on the events it raises.
Step 2. Task registration and the cyclic versus async task split.

Step 5. The top of the application layer and the module that consumes database, algorithm, balancing, SOA, measurement and diagnosis at once. It is the first point at which the database and task integration model can be judged end to end.
Step 4. The CAN driver, after its helper and before the callbacks that depend on both.

interface_boundary.description: The hardware-abstraction boundary is the set of TI HALCoGen headers the SIL harness supplies. The recorded run resolves, for every one of the 313 test targets, which HL_* headers are required through the test's own include closure and which through the module under test. 38 distinct interface headers are pulled in across the suite. This boundary is where host integration stops being evidence about the product: everything below it is a substitute.
interface_boundary.statement: Counts are from the halcogen_via_module_under_test field of each of the 313 records in the run, that is the headers the module under test itself needs, not the test's. HL_spi, HL_can and HL_het together account for the AFE and CAN trees, which is consistent with those being 155 and 163 of the outgoing edges.

dependency_basis.scope: src/app/** and src/bootloader/** .c files, 263 in total. src/os/freertos/** is excluded from the graph because it is vendored third-party code whose own test suite is upstream's concern.
tools_consulted: graft build (full repository wiring graph, 1445 files parsed)
graft skeleton <file> (signature-level API surface of individual modules and test files)
graft callers <symbol> --depth 2 (blast-radius query against the modules under test)
tools_that_returned_nothing: graft callers --depth 2 returned 'no indexed callers - the graph has no incoming call/reference edges for this symbol as written' for every symbol probed (CRC_CalculateCrc, DATA_Read1DataBlock, BMS_Init, SYS_Init, DATA_PROCESS_DATA). It also reports that each name is defined twice - once in the .c and once in the .h - and that a cross-file caller of an ambiguous name is dropped rather than guessed. The graph as built therefore carries file-level wiring and signature-level skeletons but no resolved cross-file call edges, so it could not establish what calls what. This is recorded so a later reader does not assume the question was not asked.

graft callers could not be used to derive integration order, and the #include graph was used instead. An #include edge is a coarser relation than a call edge: it over-states coupling where a header is included for a type rather than a call, and it misses a call made through a function pointer or a macro dispatch. The order derived from it is therefore conservative - it integrates more things earlier than a call graph strictly would - which is the safe direction for a plan.

widest_fan_out.note: The largest coupling surface in the tree: 33 modules reaching 21 distinct layers, including bootloader layers. CAN is not a peripheral here, it is the spine.
59 modules. Four AFE vendor trees (ADI, LTC, Maxim, NXP) plus TI and a debug default, all behind one AFE API.

The widest reach of any layer, and the reason config integration cannot be deferred: the configuration headers declare the data-block layout that every other layer compiles against. A change to battery_cell_cfg.c or battery_system_cfg.c is an interface change to the whole product.
Low fan-out and high fan-in: 22 modules in, 5 edges out. It is a leaf consumer of almost everything, which makes it the natural place to observe whether the layers below it behave.

execution_state.statement: NONE of the 9 ordered steps has been executed. This record is a plan, authored from measured repository structure, and no integration test specification or integration test result exists to execute it. Of the 5 levels, IL-01 is partially executable now and IL-02, IL-03, IL-04 and IL-05 are not executable in this corpus at all. FB2-VER-TMS-000007 is a planning stub and FB2-VER-EXE-000007 is execution_kind none with outcome blocked. record_verbatim.independence_statement: This plan was authored by an AI agent from repository sources. An AI-authored plan is not an independent plan in the ASPICE sense: nobody who did not write the modules has reviewed the ordering, the level definitions or the severity model. It has not been reviewed by a human, it is not approved, it has never been executed, and it confers no verification credit. Every level's exit criteria are unproven assertions about what would constitute sufficient evidence.

integration_levels.defect_routing: A module-level integration defect is a module defect. Route to the module's own defect record; do not open an integration defect.
entry_criteria: Each module's own unit tests build and have a recorded result, so a module-level integration failure can be attributed to integration rather than to the module.
The module's include closure resolves entirely within itself plus the HL_* interface headers.

SIL HL_* interface headers under sil/iface/

environment.substitution_and_its_limitation: The HL_* headers are CMock-generated doubles. Integrating at this level proves the module's own logic and its interface contract; it proves nothing about whether the real HALCoGen driver has the same semantics, because the double is derived from the header, and the header is the thing under suspicion in the 3 sil_interface_header_mismatch build failures.

exit_criteria: Every module in scope has a passing recorded result, or a recorded failure attributed to a named defect.
No module in scope is vacuous: each has at least one test that asserts something about its behaviour.
integration_levels.regression_selection_rule: Re-run the module's own tests plus every test that includes the module. For foxmath that is 43 modules' worth of tests by fan-in alone.

The 28 excluded-upstream files need a decision on whether they are excluded on purpose.

A layout change routes to SUP.8 configuration management, not to a defect record, because it changes the interface every other layer compiles against.
entry_criteria: IL-01 exit criteria met for the modules these six depend on: foxmath, os support, io, mcu.

environment.substitution_and_its_limitation: The host substitutes POSIX threads for FreeRTOS tasks. A task that runs at the right period on POSIX and at the wrong period on FreeRTOS is the classic divergence this substitution hides, and the corpus has no way to observe a task period at all.

exit_criteria: A data block written by one module is read by another with the payload byte-identical, demonstrated by TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_MEMORY and not by field-by-field equality.
The cyclic and async task split in ftask is exercised: a cyclic task runs on its period and an async task runs on its event, both observed rather than assumed.
The os abstraction is exercised against the FreeRTOS contract, not only against the POSIX host implementation.

integration_levels.unblock_condition: Needs a FreeRTOS host build and a task-period observation capability. Neither exists. The database unit tests give the store semantics but not the task model.

integration_order.why_this_order: These have the highest fan-in - 43, 43, and the io and mcu pair - and no obligation to be integrated after anything. Settling them first maximises the number of later steps that have one fewer unknown.

os.c has 40 inbound edges and ftask.c 22, and both are prerequisites for every task a later level runs. The os and ftask pair shares a header, which is the one file-level cycle in the graph, so they are integrated together rather than in sequence.
39 inbound edges. Nothing above it can be judged until the store and notify semantics are fixed, because almost every later step reads or writes a data block.

integration_order.dependency_basis: widest_fan_out: app/config, 51 edges, 29 distinct target layers
integration_order.why_this_order: The config layer has the widest reach in the tree at 51 outgoing edges touching 29 layers. It is integrated after database because the database's own block ids come from it, and before every producer and consumer, because a layout disagreement found late is an interface change to 29 layers.

diag.c has 32 inbound edges and 5 outgoing; can_helper.c has 38 and can.c 17. The diagnostic engine is a leaf consumer of almost everything, which makes it the first place the integration of the layers below it can be observed from outside.

integration_order.dependency_basis: spi.c 14 inbound; both include io and mcu from step 1
integration_order.why_this_order: Both are IL-01 leaves that the AFE level needs. Integrating them here rather than at step 1 keeps the AFE boundary contiguous.

integration_order.dependency_basis: widest_fan_out: app/afe 155 edges across 59 modules; HL_spi 70, HL_het 60, HL_sys_dma 27 tests
integration_order.why_this_order: One AFE vendor, end to end, before any second vendor. The 39-assertion PEC drift pin already exists here, which is the only AFE-level integration evidence the corpus has today.

integration_order.dependency_basis: GAP-UTS-003: 19 zero-test-case files in the two shared layers
integration_order.why_this_order: The remaining three vendors, only after step 7 is integrated. Deliberately last: the ADI ADES183x and NXP MC3377x shared layers have 19 test files with no test case in them, and integrating four vendors against untested shared code would multiply one defect into four.

integration_order.dependency_basis: fan_in_ranking: bms.c 17; bms.c includes bal, database, diag, soa, meas, imd, led, sps, os and config
integration_order.why_this_order: The top of the stack, and the first point at which the database and task integration model can be judged end to end. Placed last because it depends on every level below and because two of its members currently have no usable verification: test_soa.c has no outcome oracle and test_contactor.c does not build.

The module-to-module edges between them, at interface level: a data-block layout, a function signature, a diagnostic event id.
The CMock-generated interface doubles the recorded host sweep already uses, extended to the module pairs that currently have no test.
out_of_scope: The hardware-abstraction layer below the 38 HL_* interface headers. No integration of a real driver against a real peripheral is possible in this corpus.
src/os/freertos/** and the vendored FreeRTOS tree. It is third-party code; integrating against it means integrating against upstream's own test suite, not a plan authored here.

The 72 modules with no include edge at all, which are leaves by construction: the fassert, fstartup, notification, mcu, timer, rti modules and the per-vendor config tables. They are covered by the unit specification FB2-VER-UTS-000001, not by an integration plan.
Target hardware. No level below subsystem can be executed on the product's own board here.
integration_scope.scope_rationale: Scope is set by what the include graph can order and what the recorded harness can execute. The out-of-scope items are not excluded for convenience; each is excluded because the mechanism that would integrate it does not exist in this corpus, and each exclusion is restated as a blocked step below.

limitations: No step has been executed. Zero of nine. This is a plan and produces no result.

The dependency graph is an #include graph, not a call graph. graft callers --depth 2 was run against the modules under test and returned no indexed cross-file call edges for any symbol probed, so the finer relation was not available. The include graph over-states coupling where a header is included for a type, and misses dispatch through function pointers and macros. It is the conservative direction for ordering but it is not the same relation a call graph would give.

graft reported each probed symbol as defined twice, once in the .c and once in the .h, and drops cross-file callers of an ambiguous name rather than guessing. That is a second, independent reason the tool could not supply a call graph.
The 38 HL_* interface headers are counted from the halcogen_via_module_under_test field of the recorded run, which reflects the tree at the time of the run, not the current tree.
Fan-in and fan-out figures count distinct modules including a module, not call sites, and are not weighted by which header was included for which reason.

The order is a reverse topological order of an acyclic module graph. Cycles that exist at file level within a layer, the database with ftask and os with ftask header-sharing pairs, are handled by integrating the pair together, which is a judgement rather than a derivation.
No integration test specification exists, so no step here has an oracle. An order without oracles is a schedule.
record_verbatim.plan_basis: The order in this plan is derived from two measurements of the repository as it stands, not from an architectural preference. First, the include-dependency graph over all 263 .c files under src/app and src/bootloader at tree commit ebd6d5a6: for each translation unit, every #include "..." is resolved to a real header under src/ and then to that header's sibling .c, giving a directed module-to-module edge. 191 of the 263 modules have at least one such edge. Second, the per-test interface-header closure recorded in the SIL host sweep, which names the HL_* hardware-abstraction headers each test target actually requires. Those two measurements fix the order: a module is integrated after every module that includes it.

regression_selection.rule: Select by measured coupling, not by coverage, because no coverage measurement exists in this corpus. A change to module M re-runs M's own tests plus the tests of every module that includes M, computed from the include graph this plan was derived from.
regression_selection.why_not_full_regression: Because the graph gives a smaller set than the whole suite. A change to src/app/driver/foxmath/foxmath.c has 43 inbound modules and their tests are a strict subset of the 313. Running the other 270 would cost time and prove nothing about the change. The corpus has no measurement that would justify a coverage-driven selection, so a structural rule is stated instead of a percentage.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-VER-SIP-000001` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ or docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record
6. a revision_history entry whose author is the approving role and whose description records the approval and cites the signed packet

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
